Kootenai deposition in southwestern Montana was controlled by a series of complex, interrelated factors: (1) tectonic partition of the foreland into multiple basins, (2) tectonically induced base-level changes, (3) changing sedimentary sources, and (4) the interaction of these factors with the inherent fluvial geomorphic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kootenii Formation in southwestern Montana is an excellent example of a nonmarine sedimentary response to a tectonics-partitioned, foreland basin.
the Kootenain is a classic non-marine foreland basin deposit, but it is also a classic basin partitioned deposit.

the foreland basin in southwestern Montana was partitioned into several discrete depositional systems during deposition of the Kootenii Formation, and the partitioning was driven by the development of intraforeland structures.
